title: Bisphenol A and Adiposity in an Inner-City Birth Cohort.
ehr_evidence: Study subjects are participants in the prospective birth cohort of the Columbia Center for Children’s Environmental Health (CCCEH) in Northern Manhattan and the South Bronx, New York.
summary: Longitudinal birth cohort study examining associations between prenatal and early-childhood urinary bisphenol A (BPA) exposures and childhood adiposity measures (FMI, %BF, WC, BMIZ) in an inner-city NYC population.
key_findings: Prenatal urinary BPA was positively associated with age 7 FMI (β = 0.31 kg/m2; 95% CI: 0.01, 0.60, p = 0.04), %BF (β = 0.79; 95% CI: 0.03, 1.55, p = 0.04), and WC (β = 1.29 cm; 95% CI: 0.29, 2.30, p = 0.01).
Prenatal BPA was not associated with BMIZ at ages 5 or 7, or change in BMIZ between ages 5 and 7 (all p > 0.1).
The association between prenatal BPA and FMI was sex-specific, with positive associations observed in girls but not boys.
Child urinary BPA concentrations were not associated with childhood anthropometric outcomes (all p > 0.05).
Child BPA concentrations showed a borderline negative association with ΔBMIZ from 5 to 7 years (β = –0.10; 95% CI: –0.02, 0.005, p = 0.06).
captured_features: Maternal prepregnancy BMI and obesity status
population: African American and Dominican mother-child pairs in Northern Manhattan and the South Bronx, New York (children followed to age 7 years)
limitations: Use of spot urine samples leading to potential exposure misclassification due to low intraclass correlation
Lack of dietary data during pregnancy and childhood
Body composition assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis rather than gold-standard methods
Lack of pubertal timing data to account for sex-specific developmental differences
Missing anthropometric and biomarker data due to loss to follow-up
